clue.text: Restaurant reveals source of water in curry

indicators.note: in tells us the stream is placed inside the word for grooming a horse

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb
a rill is a small stream, a source of water

explanation.surface: A diner discovers where the water in its curry comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like the dish but is the verb for brushing a horse; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill room is a restaurant, or part of one, specialising in grilled food.

clue.text: Propounder of law about separating good and false

indicators.note: separating means the word for about sits between the two other pieces, keeping them apart

parts.note: sham means false or fake
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone who formulated a law on telling good money from counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: Gresham's law says bad money drives out good, so the surface's 'good and false' fits the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Gresham, Tudor financier, gave his name to the economic principle that debased coinage drives sound coin out of circulation.

clue.text: Cold? That is, extremely

indicators.note: extremely says the letters for that is go at the extremes, outside the abbreviation for cold

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A question about chilliness answered: yes, very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: frozen water is cold to an extreme degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is the very image of something extremely chilly.

clue.text: Retire before Kelly is made to rise

indicators.note: before places the word for retire ahead of the outlaw's first name

parts.note: to leave is to withdraw or retire
Ned Kelly was the notorious Australian bushranger

explanation.surface: Someone retires before a person called Kelly is made to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelly is Ned Kelly, the famous Australian outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough with yeast added is caused to swell and puff up as it proves.

clue.text: Dominant, being aware of power

parts.note: to be onto something is to be aware of it
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Being in control because you know where the power lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top means being in the controlling or winning position.

clue.text: Insect, perhaps — and article for fabre

parts.note: maybe means perhaps
et is French for and
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: An insect described, perhaps with a definite article, by the French naturalist Fabre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Fabre' says to use French, since Jean-Henri Fabre was a French entomologist: ET is French 'and', LE a French 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The May beetle, or cockchafer, is a large European beetle that appears in late spring.

clue.text: Really enjoy next stage for grub left over

indicators.note: over says the whole run is turned round, read from the far end

parts.note: a grub (larva) develops next into a pupa

explanation.surface: Devouring the leftovers is the next step for a hungry eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns PUPA + L right round. 'Grub' looks like food but is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is to relish it eagerly, like a cat drinking cream.

clue.text: Boat set in motion

explanation.surface: A boat getting under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a motor boat; to launch something is to start it off.

clue.text: Sound off in pope's office

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth inside the papal office.
explanation.definitionFit: To pontificate is to hold forth pompously; the pontificate is the office or reign of a pope.

clue.text: Pop set eyes on 25 American people

parts.note: to pop something is slang for pawning it

indicators.note: the number refers to the answer at 25 across, which means turned over, so the word for set eyes on is read backwards

parts.note: to set eyes on is to see

explanation.surface: Dad catches sight of a cross-reference to a group of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is not Dad but slang for pawn. 25 is a cross-reference: its answer, meaning turned over, reverses SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Native American nation of the Great Plains, from Nebraska and Kansas.

clue.text: Smart creature that's grand for parish boundaries

indicators.note: for signals that one thing stands in place of another

parts.note: an elephant is a creature

indicators.note: the boundaries of the word parish are its first and last letters

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A stylish animal that is a big deal around the local church district.
explanation.walkthrough: In ELEPHANT replace PH (the first and last letters of 'parish') with G.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and elegant both mean stylish and well dressed.

clue.text: Filler in conversation heard in wood? Not at all

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken aloud and the sound is what counts

parts.note: yew is a type of wood, used for longbows; no is a flat refusal, not at all

explanation.surface: Something heard in a forest: is it a conversational filler? Not in the least.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a verbal tic padding out speech, like 'um' or 'like'.

clue.text: What put back greeting for cast?

indicators.note: put back says the exclamation is reversed

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A question about what a greeting has to do with a cast of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns the questioning exclamation round; 'cast' looks theatrical but means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to throw or hurl something heavy.

clue.text: Name of mountains, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: the Appalachian mountains run down eastern North America

explanation.surface: The name of a range of mountains, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellation is a title or designation given to someone or something.

clue.text: Recommend extremely popular English writer

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of the word popular

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A tip-off: a hugely popular English author is worth reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'popular' but takes its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor recommends a treatment by ordering it formally.

clue.text: Turning up with mad poet as planned

indicators.note: turning means the following letters are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: A deranged versifier shows up, as was arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' shuffles UP and MADPOET; 'mad' is fodder, not the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mapped out has been planned in detail, like a route drawn on a chart.

clue.text: Cathode ray almost displaced solid objects

indicators.note: displaced means the letters are moved out of their places
almost says the word ray loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cathode ray has nearly been knocked off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims RAY to RA; 'displaced' shuffles CATHODE + RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solid figures with eight faces, the plural of octahedron.

clue.text: Teacher part way through term is shattered

indicators.note: part way through says the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher is worn out halfway through the term.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS is hidden in 'terM IS Shattered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils address a female teacher as Miss.

clue.text: Nameless undergrad organised militant youth

indicators.note: organised means the remaining letters are put into a new order
nameless means the word undergrad loses N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An anonymous student gets political.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N from UNDERGRAD; 'organised' rearranges UDERGRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were Mao's young militants of China's Cultural Revolution.

clue.text: Fish not in shoal?

explanation.surface: A question about a fish swimming apart from the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole is a flatfish; sole also means only, alone, as a fish outside a shoal would be.

clue.text: Expressing deep emotion like this female in opera from the south

parts.note: so means thus, like this

indicators.note: from the south in a down clue means read upwards
in places the abbreviation for female inside the opera's title

parts.note: Lulu is an opera by Alban Berg

explanation.surface: Like this female in an opera, from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the insertion into Berg's opera; 'from the south' turns the result upwards, giving ULFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Soulful music or looks are full of deep feeling.

clue.text: European politician stopping the boat rides here?

indicators.note: stopping means the politician plugs the gap between the other words

parts.note: taken as written
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's
MEP stands for Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: A Euro-MP blocking the boat: is this where the rides are?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' signals the politician plugging the phrase 'the boat'; 'rides here?' is the definition, with its question mark marking an example-style hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park is an amusement park full of rides built around a theme.

clue.text: Family doctor elected as most important person

parts.note: kin means family or relations
GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A family doctor is voted in as top dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one GP, but 'Family' gives KIN and 'doctor' GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the central or key figure in an organisation.

clue.text: Boat provided by south American god

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A boat supplied by a deity from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and the Far East.

clue.text: Beau Nash is worried by daughter lacking shame

indicators.note: worried means the letters are troubled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Beau Nash, the Regency dandy, is troubled by his daughter's brazen ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was the Georgian dandy and master of ceremonies at Bath; 'worried' scrambles his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed is not embarrassed or ashamed in the least.

clue.text: Commitment keeping Simpson primarily in Springfield

indicators.note: keeping means the larger word holds the letter within it

parts.note: a duty is a commitment or obligation

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of Simpson

explanation.surface: An obligation keeps a Simpson in Springfield, the cartoon town.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield is the Simpsons' town, but here it is Dusty Springfield, the British singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty was the stage first name of the 1960s British pop singer Mary O'Brien.

clue.text: Pick up article in valley

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the word for valley

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Collecting an item in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather or pick up bit by bit, like leftover grain.

clue.text: Us agent detaining fra filippo almost lost control

indicators.note: detaining means the agent holds the painter's name inside

parts.note: a Fed is an agent of the US FBI

indicators.note: almost means the painter's surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Fra Filippo Lippi was a Florentine Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: An American agent holds the painter Fra Filippo, then nearly goes berserk.
explanation.walkthrough: Fra Filippo Lippi was a 15th-century Florentine painter; 'almost' trims his surname and 'detaining' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To have flipped is to have gone mad or lost one's temper.

clue.text: Boat is going to work

parts.note: shall expresses the future, is going to
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A boat is about to be put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open boat for shallow water.

clue.text: Fortune for biblical refugee

explanation.surface: Fortune awaits a refugee from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's fate; Lot fled Sodom in Genesis.

clue.text: Holland, say, requiring trade name

parts.note: a line is a trade or line of business

explanation.surface: The Netherlands needs a brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: Holland is not the country but a smooth unbleached cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland is a type of plain-woven cloth, an example of this fabric.

clue.text: Reduction in sentence? Yes, and no criminal gets time inside

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for time within the jumbled letters
criminal means the letters are twisted out of their lawful order

explanation.surface: A cut in a prison term? Both yes and no: a criminal gets time inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges YESANDNO and 'inside' puts T within it. The surface's 'sentence' and 'time inside' suggest prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure of speech omits conjunctions, shortening a sentence, as in 'veni, vidi, vici'.
